issues.body: `reconcile_dispatch_head` still extracts and validates only `object.sha`; it never checks `object.type`. A payload such as `{"object":{"sha":"<40 lowercase hex>","type":"tag"}}`, or the same payload with `type` absent, is therefore accepted as the authoritative commit head. This is materially the same major finding as round 3. The new self-tests put `type: "commit"` in positive fixtures, but none changes or removes that field, so the missing trust check remains untested. Outcome-path fakes have the same blind spot because the reducer ignores their type value.
issues.fix_hint: Require `node.get("type") == "commit"` in addition to the exact 40-lowercase-hex SHA check. Add negative reducer rows for a valid SHA with `type: "tag"`, missing `type`, and another invalid type, asserting `WorkerPrError`; also drive at least one such payload through each relevant outcome path and assert `malformed-head` with no mutation.
issues.title: Branch-ref reducer still accepts non-commit Git objects

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-3 trust failure remains unchanged. The reducer still validates only the SHA syntax and never verifies the Git object's `type`, despite its contract and callers treating the returned value as a commit. The added fixtures include `type: "commit"` on successful payloads but do not add the requested negative tag/missing-type cases, so they cannot detect this defect.
